anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves five facts and loses none. In A, B and E, row 1 is now accept contract change, grounded in the reread ticket (A), the impossibility of offline search against a hosted index (B) and the retained step-2 copy when the reread fails (E); Before recommended preserve in all three by deferring to the spec at the reviewed head. In D the third sentence now says outright that the linked ticket could not be read and that it is therefore unknown whether green serves a goal blue cannot; Before's last sentence only said "no readable ticket", which I judged too oblique to count as naming the failed read, though this was the closest call. The message fact now holds because every menu quotes both wordings and then gives exactly three sentences (obligation, gain or cost naming the ticket where one decides, pick with reason), with no tracker IDs, neutral row descriptions and stop last; Before used two or three paragraphs of argument. C and F kept their preserve recommendations and reasons (the index is fast across seven years; the ticket requires a live check on every open, in the second sentence). To keep this stable, hold the wording that fixes the sentence roles: sentence two carries the ticket's requirement whenever a ticket decides, and sentence three carries the failed read only when nothing else decides. D's second sentence is the weakest: it states an absence of a goal rather than a gain or cost, so say there that with an unreadable ticket the sentence should state what the change would cost or fail to gain for any stated goal. Keep tracker IDs confined to the fetch narration outside the menu, as A and C do now.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved ticket, necessary and fallback by judging the proposal from the reread ticket (A), from whether the goal is achievable under the current wording (B), and from the retained step-2 copy when the reread fails (E); Before defaulted to preserve in all three, pending explicit authorization. It moved unknown by putting the failed read and the missing evidence of necessity into D's third sentence rather than only in the fetch narration. It moved message by quoting the current and proposed wording as a pair, holding the explanation to three sentences with no tracker IDs, and stripping the row labels of argument (Before's rows said things like "the offline-search goal remains blocked" and "retain the obstacle to offline opening"). Viable and veto held in both, so nothing regressed. One thing to tighten: the second sentence names the ticket in A, E and F but not in C, where it mentions only the index and the lookup target. That is defensible because the ticket is silent on retention, but if you want the fact to be robust, have the wording say the second sentence names the ticket whenever one was read (e.g. "the ticket asks only for faster lookup, which an index delivers without deleting receipts"). Keep the rule that a ticket's explicit requirement vetoes the PR's goal, as in F, and keep the row labels neutral.
